[q="COMaestro"]Did this TTS matchup ever happen? I'm curious to know the results.[/q]

 2-0 So far in favor of Medusa. Second one was close with a 2 health difference. We're trying to arrange for the end of the best of 5 one way or the other. The matchup is quite boring with the best tactic being getting in a few big blows and wait for decks to be empty for the fatigue damage. Matches are loooooooooooooong.


Vtyler98 is a very good and tactical player, and sure knows how to play Arthur. If we switched characters, I'd probably feel the pain for weeks.

articles.body:
It's been fun so far! First match was more figuring out the strategy Saduhem uses with Medusa, it is a bit different than the people I play with and definitely caught me off guard. Second match was super close, I had Excalibur and kept trying to go in for the kill but the Harpies were blocking me from doing that and I ran out of cards before I could kill the last few off and died due to exhaustion. Pretty crazy to not even use Excalibur once in that match and have it so close like that. There were a few things I could have done differently in that match (like keep Merlin alive, had a decision to do damage with scheme and lose him vs holding him back with 1 health and use Excalibur sooner) that might have changed things up, but it was definitely a winnable game for KA and came down to the wire! I know Saduhem hates the "command the storms" card everytime I deploy it 🙂

I'm going to deploy my traditional strategy in the next matches we play and see how that works out. What is unique about this game is how someone can play the same characters so differently.

[q="msw7c"]Glad to hear you guys are making this happen! It is only a five game sample but given both of you are very good, competitive players, I still think it’s the closest we’re getting to an expert demo of KA against one of his toughest opponents. If you ever record or stream one of these games, let us know and I’ll bring the popcorn![/q]

I believe Saduhem mentioned that he might have been recording on TTS but I'm not sure, I'm pretty new to TTS so still learning the ropes myself. The second match is what I would consider representative of what KA is capable of. Lady of the lake and excalibur were never used and it came down to the wire with Medusa prevailing but every chance for KA to pull the win out as well. That's how most of my matches with him are, he either wins or if he loses it is usually very close. The only two blowouts I have had with him were the 1st match vs Medusa since the strategy used by Saduhem is much different than how others I play with use Medusa and required some adjustment and then vs Sherlock when KA absolutely wreaked him. It is actually pretty rare that I have blow out matches when playing Unmatched in general though, most matches are usually pretty close. 

I also noticed KA has been ticking up in the spreadsheet, from under 30% to now around 32%. I am assuming some of that is coming from people playing him vs the new cobble & fog characters where he seems to match up very well. Invisible man for example has no sidekick and no feint ability to thwart KA, I haven't tried this matchup but I feel like it would be a massive advantage for KA because you could boost any attack against IM and use Merlin's ranged attacks and command the storms to manipulate IM as well. Sherlock I played vs KA and he got wreaked, not sure why but it seems like his defense cards didn't work very well against Arthur and Watson was eliminated quickly due to aggressive attacking early on. I'm not sure how Jekyll/Hyde or Dracula would match up, I think Dracula would be the toughest with his sisters, ability to heal and beastform card. 

Also, I'd love to see one of the developers like Justin play as KA, that would be really cool to see.

articles.body:
So the best of 5 between Medusa and King Arthur concluded with 3-0 for Medusa. 

I could not record the entire match every time because I don't currently have enough space available but, every single time there could have even remotely been a suspicion of cheating I recorded the previous 5 minutes. This was for both sides. Tabletop Simulator is great but isn't perfect, and pressing a key while hovering over something can mess things up. The recordings were entirely there to make sure they were available to both parties for any possible doubt. 

With that disclaimer out of the way, this is my quick and dirty description of the 3 matches. Keep in mind that this is from my perspective as Medusa and that the actions I took are much more salient in the descriptions:

1 - Fairly typical. Medusa damages and kites all game, Arthur gets an attack in when he can, which is either once or twice. Harpies are used as sources of discards and shields. Ends up with fatigue finishing Arthur off.

2 - Both players very cagey. Every single point of damage to Medusa is dealt by Merlin in the first few turns of the game. Once Merlin is dead, Medusa receives no damage. Arthur takes advantage of the big difference in health and runs to the other side of the map to win by fatigue. Medusa uses Harpies to lock Arthur in, gets in 1 attack + 4 guaranteed damage from momentary glance + Guaranteed damage from front of the card. At this point I have math on my side, and with much higher speed and boost, I run away putting my last Harpy as a roadblock. Medusa survives with 2 health. 

3 - Arthur has what I believe one of the strongest possible openings with Command the storms to split Medusa from her Harpies (which are blocked by both Arthur and Merlin) + Excalibur + Boost. Merlin also gets to damage Medusa and Kill a Harpy with a single cast of restless spirits. Arthur also gets to take Excalibur back with Lady of the Lake. Medusa kites and deals ticks of damage with ranged attacks and her passive ability  until Winged Frenzy allows the Harpies to rejoin her side. Arthur keeps drawing to make up for the discards, Medusa instead uses Snipes and Regroups to boost movement so Arthur can't catch up. In short Medusa is drawing at a much slower rate while provoking a ton of discards. She's also moving all around the board with higher base movement and higher boost values across all cards.
Arthur and Merlin have Medusa sandwiched with Excalibur in hand, but the game ends with Medusa forcing discards and killing Merlin who cannot defend on an empty hand and moving away with Dash. Arthur draws his last card and attempts to kill a Harpy without success. Medusa has plenty of cards to draw from. Arthur can't play without cards in hand or deck and with fatigue hitting twice per round. 

I think Arthur boosted 2-4 attacks across 3 games? Probably less, definitely not more.


I want to point out that Vtyler98 was absolutely phenomenal and a scary Arthur, which even more than before leads me to believe that Medusa just has a heck of a lot more (And better) tools to use. 

In conclusion, yes, I believe this is a one-sided matchup, heavily skewed towards Medusa. This doesn't mean Medusa is always going to win by a wide margin, but that Medusa will win a huge percentage of the time.
If someone wants to try the same out with Bigfoot vs Arthur, I think it'll turn out the same. Arthur gets bullied by these two guys, and giving him someone to bully in a different box isn't what I would consider balance.

With all that said, I think this all exercise is going to turn out pointless anyway.

Anecdotal reports about Arthur's issues were dismissed. Sure.
Arthur hasn't advanced a single bracket in the monthly tournaments on these board. But that doesn't meant anything apparently.
The first giant conglomerate or reported results were dismissed as, for some reason, the product of "inexperienced players". 
The data grows to 4 digits, still showing the same thing. Again, it's the "inexperienced players".
People requested "experienced players" to duke it out. Not sure if I'm "experienced", but Vtyler98 sure is, and we got straight sets for Medusa. But this won't matter either.

And you know what? There's going to be a time where someone actually wins a series with Arthur (Very likely having to do with something shown by the producing company) and that one instance is going to be the "evidence", while months worth of combined efforts are just ignored.

Can it really, really be that people that find these matchups to be unbalanced are all "inexperienced" players? That's a LOT of folks!
Can it possible be that the one thing they all have in common is the inability to play this character correctly?

Should we, for once instead, consider that maybe the one thing all these people actually do have in common, [b]The game[/b], could be at fault here? 

Anyway, if anything, the frustration with the balance in Unmatched drove me (and my gaming group) back to painting and playing what I consider to be properly tested Skirmish games (and rediscover the love of Malifaux) again, and our local meta has expanded by orders of magnitude after that. 

I wanted to do the Bigfoot series too but I'm just so, so tired of having the developer himself say that the game doesn't have balance issues and that people just don't know how to play Arthur (Or that Medusa and Bigfoot are just fine). I'll check the boards now and again and check if poor old Arthur gets a more dignified treatment, but I'm really too tired for all this.

articles.body:
Good summary of the matches, it was definitely fun playing against someone who is very good with Medusa and uses her abilities and cards to the fullest extent strategically. Thanks Saduhem for teaching me how to use TTS and I can say your tactics with Medusa were brilliant! 

I think the toughest part with Medusa is her ability to use her harpies to shield her from damage (from Arthur) and the higher movement she has. Once Merlin dies then Arthur is very one dimensional against her and it’s really tough to pull a win off especially if she has all or most of her harpies left. Trapping her is difficult because she can use her scheme card to maneuver out of those situations or her discard defense cards to force the opponent to disengage. 

The two most effective strategies for me were in games 2 and 3. Game 2 was mainly use Merlin to deal damage and force Medusa to discard cards by using command the storms to move her out of range and as far away as possible when there was a full hand of cards or close to one. Once he died though it came down to the wire but the extra movement and boost of Medusa was too much for Arthur. Game 3 I tried using command the storms on the Sarpedon map, forcing the harpies on one side and blocking each bridge with Arthur and Merlin. It worked very well until the scheme was deployed bringing back another harpy and moving them through my fighters. This made it tough for Arthur to get off his Excalibur attack and discards from attacking the harpies made it worse... then things quickly went downhill from there once Merlin died. 

I will say that I was not able to use an aggressive boosting attack strategy against Medusa. The main reason was due to the harpies always being in the way and if I chose to attack them aggressively then I’m wasting damage that needs to be used on Medusa, especially since she can bring some harpies back. 

Overall though despite how the matches turned out, I still enjoy playing as King Arthur and he’s still my favorite character in the game. Why? I love what Merlin can do, I like the option to be very aggressive with Arthur if you can line things up right and I like his play style in general. I enjoy playing with characters that can be aggressive attacking but also a little tougher to win with (Jekyll/Hyde, Arthur, Bruce Lee) vs playing with characters that are “easier” to use and win with like Bigfoot and Medusa. I love the challenge of taking an underdog like Arthur or Bruce Lee and trying to beat Bigfoot or Medusa. I guess it all comes down to one’s perspective and what they like in the game, and for me unmatched is a ton of fun to play even if some characters are harder to win with or have certain matchups that are just really tough. 

I would love to see a match with Justin playing KA vs Medusa, perhaps he and Saduhem can line that up and we can watch it? I would definitely love to see them play and see Justin using KA. Perhaps when Justin returns a match via TTS or livestream can be arranged.

articles.body:
This might sound like a dumb question but I am trying to be as technical as possible here.  King Arthur's hero card says:
[q]"When King Arthur attacks, you may BOOST that attack. Play the BOOST card, face down, along with your attack card. [b][u]If your opponent cancels the effects on your attack card[/u][/b], the BOOST is discarded without effect."[/q]

If you were to attack with Excalibur and boost it, then your opponent plays Feint, would it really make you discard your boost card?  Excalibur [b][u]doesn't have any effects[/u][/b] on it, thus Feint technically [b][u]did not cancel any effects[/u][/b], thus it would seem that King Arthur shouldn't have to discard his boost card in this one rare case.  Is this a legitimate reading of King Arthur's power?

Play the BOOST card, face down, along with your attack card. <strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">If your opponent cancels the effects on your attack card</span></strong>, the BOOST is discarded without effect."</safehtml></qbody></quote><safehtml>If you were to attack with Excalibur and boost it, then your opponent plays Feint, would it really make you discard your boost card?  Excalibur <strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">doesn't have any effects</span></strong> on it, thus Feint technically <strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">did not cancel any effects</span></strong>, thus it would seem that King Arthur shouldn't have to discard his boost card in this one rare case.  Is this a legitimate reading of King Arthur's power?</safehtml></xml>

articles.body:
With that kind of game, it seems impossible to have a perfectly balanced fight for every possible configuration. Medusa is obviously a very tough opponent for KA. Maybe we could try what is done on many popular e-games:
   - for tournaments: each player brings at least 3 teams - before selection, each player can ban 1 or two teams - then each player selects a valid team for this game
   - for casual play: each player ban one or two teams, but you can play with a banned team, you just start with -2 on your max health (if you have only 4 character, you cannot ban 2 of them...).
We could argue that Medusa and Bigfoot will always be banned, but I am not sure of that. If I want to play with Robin Hood for example, I think I will ban other characters.

With that kind of rules, maybe every character is playable with a raisonnable win-rate.
